clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old woman presented with a femur fracture due to an accident. She was alert on arrival but developed sleepiness approximately 5 hours later. Two days post-fracture, she presented with severe neurological deficits (GCS 4, positive bilateral Babinski, Kernig, neck stiffness), hypoxemia (PO2 64 mm Hg), tachycardia (HR 124 bpm), and elevated blood pressure. Imaging at this time showed a left femoral comminuted fracture, bilateral lung exudative lesions and pleural effusion on CT, and diffuse abnormal signals suggestive of embolization in the brain on MRI. Petechiae were not reported. Laboratory tests were ordered but no results were documented. Fourteen days after the fracture, lung symptoms and CT findings improved. Fifteen days post-fracture, transthoracic echocardiography revealed shunts through a patent foramen ovale (PFO). The patient was discharged with dysphasia and an untreated closed fracture, after receiving active supportive care and hormone therapy.
